indication: Adult patients with previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) with no known 17p deletion
headline: Lilly says the approval allows Jaypirca to be used as a first-line treatment for appropriate patients with CLL or SLL. It was already approved for relapsed or refractory CLL/SLL in adults previously treated with a covalent BTK inhibitor and, under accelerated approval, for relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma after at least two lines of systemic therapy including a BTK inhibitor. Recommended dose: 200 mg orally once daily (FDA).
pdufa_note: The FDA's approval notification is dated October 2, 2026 and states the approval was made that day; Eli Lilly and Company announced it the same day (Lilly's announcement). The approval is based on BRUIN CLL-313 (NCT05023980), a randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial in 282 patients with previously untreated CLL/SLL without deletion of chromosome 17p, comparing pirtobrutinib (141 patients, until disease progression) with bendamustine plus a rituximab product (141 patients, six cycles). Per the FDA, progression-free survival assessed by an independent review committee had a hazard ratio of 0.20 (95% CI 0.11 to 0.37; p<0.0001); median progression-free survival was not estimable in the pirtobrutinib arm and 33.5 months in the bendamustine and rituximab arm, at an estimated median follow-up of 28 months. Overall survival data were immature: 3 deaths (2.1%) in the pirtobrutinib arm and 10 (7.1%) in the control arm at the primary analysis. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 28% of patients taking pirtobrutinib, and the most common non-laboratory adverse reactions (20% or more) were upper respiratory tract infections, rash and COVID-19. Pirtobrutinib received orphan drug designation. In June 2026 Lilly said it had submitted its CLL results (BRUIN CLL-313 and CLL-314) to the FDA, "with a decision expected in the second half of 2026" (Lilly, June 26, 2026); pdufa.bio holds no goal date, so no early or late margin is computed. Earlier FDA approvals of Jaypirca: January 27, 2023 (relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma after at least two lines of systemic therapy including a BTK inhibitor, accelerated approval), December 1, 2023 (CLL/SLL after at least two prior lines including a BTK inhibitor and a BCL-2 inhibitor, accelerated approval) and December 3, 2025 (traditional approval for adults with relapsed or refractory CLL/SLL previously treated with a covalent BTK inhibitor). The FDA's approval letter for this supplement (NDA 216059) had not yet been posted on Drugs@FDA when this page was published.
source_label: FDA approval notification, pirtobrutinib for previously untreated CLL or SLL, October 2, 2026
